tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on observable symptoms/user-reported scenarios rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists trigger contexts (error codes, symptoms, even the case where 'the user only says one update keeps failing'), and remains a single tight paragraph despite covering many edge cases.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Windows Server EC2 instance's update mechanism works but a specific patch fails because of the component it targets or the host's role... Apply it to classify and fix the failure.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific error codes, component-specific fixes, and AWS/Nitro-specific driver behavior without explaining general concepts the agent would already know. It's dense and information-rich without filler.
tests.evidence: Windows Update pushes a generic driver that overrides the AWS-specific driver, breaking network or the boot volume on Nitro.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed per-component procedures in separate reference files (driver-conflicts.md, dotnet-repair.md, etc.) and only includes short diagnostic commands and summarized guidance inline. No large reference tables or lookup data are embedded in the body.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: High-risk operations (driver exclusion, cluster node draining) are given exact, prescriptive commands and explicit warnings, while classification and routing allow some diagnostic flexibility — the calibration matches fragility appropriately.
tests.evidence: Never reboot the last online node; prefer Cluster-Aware Updating. **High-risk.**

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple approaches exist (e.g., driver fix), the skill designates one clear default action (exclude from WU, don't reinstall generic driver) rather than listing equal options.
tests.evidence: The fix is to **exclude drivers from WU** ... NOT to reinstall a generic driver.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification-then-route procedure applicable to any instance exhibiting these symptoms, rather than a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the failing component (read-only) ... Step 2: Route to the component (load the matching reference)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious environment-specific pitfalls (WU drivers breaking EC2, cluster quorum loss, WSUS misconfiguration) that the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: Windows Update drivers can break EC2 — a generic WU driver over the AWS ENA/NVMe/PV driver causes BSOD or a lost boot volume on Nitro.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: This skill is primarily a diagnostic/remediation procedure, not a report-generation task, so there is no strong need for an output template; the Validation section covers the needed structured checks.
tests.evidence: The skill's purpose is to classify and fix a failure, not produce a formatted report, so templates are not required.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body

tests.evidence: No templates present in the body — passes by absence.
